why_it_matters: Ramps, rooftops, photos you zoom and a flagpole's shadow all rely on one fact: making a triangle bigger never changes its angle ratios.

concepts.text: Triangles with the same angles are the same shape, just zoomed in or out (similar triangles)
When you scale a triangle both sides scale together, so opposite ÷ hypotenuse stays the same
So you can use it: at 30° a ramp always rises 0.5 of its slope length, so a 10 ft ramp rises 5 ft

misconception: A bigger triangle has a bigger sine, so sin 30° is 0.5 in my small triangle but 1 in a triangle twice as big
root_prerequisite: Similar triangles: same shape, different size

boss.name: Sir Cosine Overreach
boss.backstory: A swan in a velvet cape who carries a sign reading 'BIGGER TRIANGLE, BIGGER SINE' and inflates every ratio he meets.

taunt: I have enlarged the triangle. The sine has been enlarged accordingly.
One does not simply keep a ratio. One improves it.
Observe the size of my triangle. Now observe the size of my sine.
heal: Splendid. Grander triangles yield grander sines. I shall have it engraved.
Precisely. Bigger is better, even in trigonometry.
hit: This is most irregular. My ratio appears to have remained unchanged.
I did not authorize a second triangle of identical proportions.
lines.reformed: I have rechecked at three sizes. The ratio did not move. I would like to join you.

cliffhanger: I heard sine and cosine, squared and added, always make exactly 1. Even for weird angles. That can't be right… right?

quiz.question: Two right triangles have the same angles, but one is twice as big. Same shape or different shape, and what changed?
quiz.answer: Same shape (similar). Every side is twice as long; the angles did not change.

quiz.question: A 30° triangle has opposite 3 and hypotenuse 6. A bigger 30° triangle has hypotenuse 12. What is sin 30° in the big one?
quiz.answer: 0.5. Its opposite is 6, and 6 ÷ 12 = 0.5, the same as 3 ÷ 6.

quiz.question: A ramp makes a 30° angle and is 10 ft long along the slope. How high does it rise?
